requirement: Prove flush semantics and document the exact durability boundary the browser can actually guarantee.

dedicatedBrowserVerification.exactClaim: canonical payload and manifest writes complete SyncAccessHandle.flush(), then close(), and a fresh authority reopens/verifies the same canonical bytes

exactBoundary: Canonical browser checkpoint payload is written in a dedicated worker with createSyncAccessHandle({mode:'readwrite'}).
The worker truncates, writes the complete byte payload, truncates to final length, calls flush(), then calls close().
Only after the payload flush/close succeeds may canonical manifest publication execute.
The canonical manifest itself uses the same explicit flush/close path.
A fresh checkpoint authority reopens the OPFS workspace and verifies the same canonical sequence, digest and complete bytes.
explicitNonClaims: No claim of power-loss durability stronger than the browser SyncAccessHandle flush contract.
No claim about hardware/filesystem/controller cache persistence not exposed by the Web API.
No claim that browser-managed OPFS is immune to eviction, user deletion or device failure.
